title: gc: purge swallows the slice stop failure, then deletes every unit file (same hazard as pctl-8sd)
lifecycle: apply_row's [Removed] arm still swallows every Pctl_error, not just no-such-unit
description:
Pre-existing; found while reviewing pctl-8sd, which narrowed the sibling site.

lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:116-117:
    | Schema.Removed -> (
        try M.stop_unit handle ~unit:unit_s
        with Schema.Pctl_error _ -> ())

The module header (lifecycle.ml:15-17) justifies this as "systemd may have already GCed the unit after its file was deleted" — and the reload path does delete the file first (lifecycle.ml:149-152 removes Removed rows from the unit store before apply_plan, and apply_plan daemon_reloads before stopping). So a no-such-unit reply here is genuinely expected.

But the catch is not limited to that. A transport failure, a bus disconnect, or a stop that systemd refuses is swallowed identically — and by then the unit FILE IS ALREADY GONE, so the still-running process is orphaned with no unit left to manage it. The excuse covers "unit was GCed", not "the bus died".

Fix: narrow to `with Schema.Pctl_error e when Schema.is_no_such_unit e -> ()` (the predicate added by pctl-8sd) and update the header bullet to say no-such-unit only. Add an integration case arming fail_next_stop on a Removed service row with a non-NoSuchUnit reply and asserting it propagates.

title: systemctl/dbus: three sites comment 'NoSuchUnit tolerance' but swallow every Pctl_error, so a bus failure reads as a unit state
description:
Pre-existing; found while reviewing pctl-8sd, which added Schema.is_no_such_unit.

Three sites in lib/systemctl/dbus.ml catch `Schema.Pctl_error _` and substitute a value that reads as a legitimate answer:

- :635 — unit_state: `try Some (get_unit_path t ~unit:u) with Schema.Pctl_error _ -> None` → Schema.Inactive. Comment says "GetUnit may fail with NoSuchUnit for a unit that has never been loaded ... We treat any exception on get_unit_path as inactive."
- :682-689 — unit_job_pending: same get_unit_path catch → false, plus `with Schema.Pctl_error _ -> false` around read_job_path. Comment: "Same NoSuchUnit tolerance as [unit_state]".
- :695 — safe_unit_state_forward: `try unit_state t ~unit:u with Schema.Pctl_error _ -> Schema.Inactive`.

In each case a bus disconnect, a transport errno, or a malformed reply is indistinguishable from "the unit is not loaded". `pctl status` then reports inactive for a service that is actually running; the wait loop sees no pending job and can conclude early.

Fix: narrow all three to `when Schema.is_no_such_unit e` and let everything else propagate. :695 is the signal-handler forward and may genuinely need to not raise — if so, keep a catch there but log the reply rather than silently returning Inactive.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
Concrete instance, observed 2026-08-02 during the pctl-jbd verification run. Details and the journal are in pctl-xxf's comment; the short version:

A 'switch-to-configuration' reexec landed while test_depends_on_wait's 'app' unit was queued-Inactive behind its migrate dependency. unit_job_pending's two 'with Schema.Pctl_error _ -> false' catches (dbus.ml) turned the peer-gone reply into 'no pending job'. Probe then read Inactive + no-job as terminal and pctl exited 5 with 'service app terminated in state inactive' — for a service systemd started successfully one second later.

This is exactly the failure mode this ticket describes ('the wait loop sees no pending job and can conclude early'), with a real trigger rather than a hypothetical one. The transient was indistinguishable from a unit state, as predicted.

title: cli/pipeline: down ~quiet:true maps every failure to exit 0, so a propagated stop failure reports success
description:
Pre-existing, but pctl-8sd makes it consequential: Lifecycle.down now propagates a non-no-such-unit slice stop failure, and this site erases it.

lib/cli/pipeline.ml:292-295:
    if quiet then
      try
        work ();
        0
      with _ -> 0
    else run work

`with _ -> 0` is broader than Pctl_error — it swallows Failure, Sys_error, Not_found, everything — and returns the success exit code.

Sole caller is test/e2e/harness.ml:209 teardown, which additionally wraps it in `try ... with _ -> ()`. So the observable effect today is that e2e teardown cannot fail: a project whose slice would not stop leaves its units on disk and its processes running on the dev's session, and the test suite reports green. That is the 'Straggler' failure mode UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:91 already names, with the one signal that would have caught it discarded.

Fix: decide what quiet means. If it means "don't print", drop the catch entirely and let the exit code carry the failure. If teardown genuinely must not abort, catch in the harness (which already does) and have it print the rendered error rather than swallowing at the pipeline layer. Either way the double swallow should collapse to one deliberate site.

title: systemctl fakes: In_mem raises op="stop" where Dbus raises op="StopUnit", so integration assertions match a label no real error carries
description:
Pre-existing; surfaced by pctl-8sd's new integration test.

lib/systemctl/in_mem.ml:116 raises Unit_op_failed { op = "stop"; ... }.
lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:529 is `let stop_unit t ~unit:u = call_unit_op t ~op:"StopUnit" ~unit:u`, so the real adapter raises op = "StopUnit".

test/integration/test_lifecycle.ml (test_down_propagates_stop_failure) asserts
`Schema.Pctl_error (Schema.Unit_op_failed { op = "stop"; _ })` — correct against the fake, but it pins a label that never appears in production, so the assertion cannot catch a change in what the real adapter reports, and any code that ever matches on `op` would be tested against the wrong string.

Per CLAUDE.md the fake is a port adapter standing in for the real one; a value it fabricates differently from the real adapter is a recorded-double drift.

Check the other In_mem ops for the same divergence (start/restart/daemon_reload) and align them on the Dbus method names (StartUnit, StopUnit, RestartUnit, Reload). Then update the integration assertion.

title: schema: Unit_op_failed should carry the D-Bus error name as its own field, so classification is equality rather than a prefix test on a display string
description:
Follow-on from pctl-8sd, which the ticket itself scoped to [reply] ("Unit_op_failed carries [reply], which holds the D-Bus error name"). The predicate works, but it classifies on a string built for humans.

lib/schema/schema.ml:466-471:
    let is_no_such_unit = function
      | Unit_op_failed { reply; _ } ->
          String.starts_with ~prefix:no_such_unit_dbus_error reply
      | _ -> false

Two consequences:

1. lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:339-344 (format_bus_reply) has four arms, and only two put the name first:
       | Some name, Some message -> sprintf "%s: %s" name message
       | None, Some message -> message
       | Some name, None -> name ^ " (no message)"
       | None, None -> format_sd_bus_err op rc
   The `None, Some message` arm emits a bare message with no name at all. A NoSuchUnit reaching that arm classifies as "propagate". The direction is safe, but the classifier is coupled to a formatting function it cannot see, and the coupling is invisible at the call site in lifecycle.

2. lib/schema/schema.ml holds a D-Bus wire constant (no_such_unit_dbus_error) although schema is the pure core and knows nothing about the transport. The prefix test also has no terminator, so a hypothetical org.freedesktop.systemd1.NoSuchUnitXxx would be tolerated (no such systemd error name exists today).

Fix: add `error_name : string option` to Unit_op_failed, populated in dbus.ml from Sd_bus_error.parts (None for transport failures, which is the correct "propagate" answer) and set explicitly by In_mem. is_no_such_unit becomes an equality test on that field; [reply] stays for rendering only. This makes the misclassification unrepresentable instead of merely unlikely.

comments.author: claude
manveru
comments.text:
Adjacent, same root cause: Dbus.daemon_reload's retry-exhaustion detail is also stringly-typed into the same field.

lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:577-583 appends '(gave up after %d attempts over %.1fs)' to `reply` before raising Unit_op_failed. A caller that wants to distinguish 'rejected immediately' from 'burned the full 5s budget' -- Gc.opportunistic_sweep is the one that most wants to, since it swallows the error and pays the latency -- has to substring-match a display string, which is exactly what this ticket says about the error name.

If Unit_op_failed grows a typed name field, consider whether it should also carry the attempt count and elapsed time rather than having them formatted into `reply`.

Noted during the round-4 review of pctl-jbd; the string form was implemented as round 1 requested, so it is not a defect in that diff.

title: e2e harness: slice_name/service_name sprintf the unit-name convention under a comment claiming they delegate to Schema
description:
Pre-existing; found while reviewing pctl-8sd.

test/e2e/harness.ml:500-504:
    (* Name helpers — delegate to the canonical Schema derivations so tests
     * and production agree on the filename convention. *)
    let slice_name id_s = Printf.sprintf "pctl-%s.slice" id_s
    let service_name id_s svc = Printf.sprintf "pctl-%s-%s.service" id_s svc

The comment is true of slice_filename_for/service_filename_for immediately below (which do call Schema.Unit_filename) and false of these two, which hardcode the convention. So tests and production agree only by coincidence, and a change to Schema.Unit_filename would leave these silently stale — the exact drift the comment claims to prevent.

They also duplicate the pair below: slice_name (Project_id.to_string id) and slice_filename_for ~id return the identical string, which is why pctl-8sd's new e2e test carries both an `id_s`/`slice` pair and a `slice_file`.

Fix: delete slice_name/service_name and have callers use slice_filename_for/service_filename_for, or reimplement them in terms of Schema.Unit_filename. Then update the affected e2e tests.

title: systemctl/dbus: only daemon_reload survives a peer-gone window; every other bus call still fails
description:
Follow-on from pctl-jbd, which scoped the retry to Manager.Reload because Reload is idempotent.

The trigger is not specific to Reload. `switch-to-configuration` (every NixOS / home-manager activation) runs `systemctl --user daemon-reexec`; the user manager drops its bus connection and dbus-broker answers every in-flight call to it with org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.NoReply 'Remote peer disconnected' (driver_goodbye, dbus-broker src/bus/driver.c:2579). Until the manager re-registers, calls get ServiceUnknown / NameHasNoOwner instead.

Unprotected sites in lib/systemctl/dbus.ml, all reachable from a single `pctl up`:
  - call_unit_op :519 -> start_unit / stop_unit / restart_unit
  - manager_subscribe :542 (Subscribe)
  - get_unit_path :576 (GetUnit)
  - read_active_state :591 and the Job read at :656 (Properties.Get)

So a rebuild racing `pctl up` no longer fails at the reload, but can still fail at StartUnit. Measured on this host (systemd 260, dbus-broker 37) with a scratch harness that reloaded 40 times while reexec'ing 4 times: 4/4 reexecs produced the failure with the retry disabled, 0/4 with it enabled — the same window applies to any call made in it.

Deciding what to do needs one judgement per op, which is why it was not folded into pctl-jbd:
  - StartUnit/StopUnit/RestartUnit are issued with mode 'replace', so re-issuing is safe, but a retry after a disconnect cannot tell whether the first job was enqueued. Probably still correct to retry; wants a deliberate call.
  - The read-only ops (GetUnit, Properties.Get) are trivially safe to retry.
  - manager_subscribe is called during connect setup; a retry there interacts with install_match_rule_and_fiber.

Bus_retry.with_retry / is_peer_gone already exist and are unit-tested (test/unit/test_bus_retry.ml); this is about choosing the sites, not new machinery.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
Two things to fold in when the sites listed here get touched.

1. The with_error/with_reply/check_rc scaffold is now repeated at seven sites in lib/systemctl/dbus.ml — :520, :540 (the new daemon_reload attempt), :568, :578, :592, :602, :617, :675 — i.e. essentially the exact list this ticket enumerates. call_unit_op already extracts one instance for start/stop/restart; the rest are inline copies. Wrapping each one in a retry individually would duplicate the retry too. Extract a single 'call ~op ~unit ~args' that returns the raw (rc, name, reply) triple, put the Bus_retry wrapper on that one function, and the per-op judgement this ticket asks for becomes a flag on the call rather than seven edits.

2. daemon_reload's retry uses Unix.gettimeofday for its deadline (dbus.ml:555), which is CLOCK_REALTIME. lib/probe/probe.ml:75-81 is the repo's existing deadline code and is monotonic throughout ('mono_now env = Eio.Time.Mono.now (env#mono_clock :> ...)'). Dbus.connect (dbus.ml:472) is 'let connect ~sw _env' — it already receives the env carrying mono_clock and discards it. Whichever sites get wrapped, thread env#mono_clock onto Dbus.t once rather than repeating the realtime call; that also drops the 'unix' library that pctl-jbd added to lib/systemctl/dune solely for gettimeofday (it is the only Unix use in the whole library).

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
Observed in the wild, not theoretical. This bit during the pctl-jbd verification run on 2026-08-02.

scripts/e2e-repeat.sh 3 came back 2/3. Run 3 failed in test_depends_on_wait:

  ASSERT up --wait exit=5
  systemctl wait app failed: service app terminated in state 'inactive' (expected 'active')

User journal, same second:

  00:32:44 Created slice pctl slice for project_4c9e86b8.
  00:32:45 Starting pctl service migrate for project_4c9e86b8...
  00:32:45 Reexecution requested from client PID 3432855 ('switch-to-confi')...
  00:32:45 Reexecuting.
  00:32:46 Finished pctl service migrate ... / Started pctl service app ...

Attribution is unambiguous — reexecs in that window, by client comm:
  4x 'systemctl'        <- test_reload_survives_reexec's own kicker, runs 1 and 2
  1x 'switch-to-confi'  <- a NixOS/home-manager activation, run 3

So a rebuild landed mid-run again, and this time it did NOT hit Reload (now retried) but the probe's property reads, which are the sites this ticket is about.

Exact chain:
  1. app is queued-Inactive behind migrate (Requires=/After=).
  2. Probe classifies Inactive as `Maybe_terminal and asks unit_job_pending.
  3. unit_job_pending (dbus.ml) is get_unit_path + read_job_path, and BOTH are wrapped in 'with Schema.Pctl_error _ -> false'. The peer-gone reply is swallowed.
  4. Probe sees Inactive + no pending job -> terminal -> reports 'terminated in state inactive'.
  5. pctl exits 5 on a service that started fine one second later.

That is this ticket (the read ops are unprotected) compounded by pctl-q2j (the catch is wider than the NoSuchUnit tolerance its comment claims). Either fix alone would have turned this into a retry or a loud transport error instead of a wrong unit state. Worth doing them together.

Note the read ops are trivially safe to retry — they have no side effects — so of the sites listed in this ticket they are the cheapest to fix and, on this evidence, the highest value.

title: pctl issues two Manager.Reload calls per command (~540ms each), four per up+down round trip
description:
Observed while investigating pctl-jbd, from the user journal on this host (systemd 260):

  Jul 30 22:21:24 systemd[20455]: Reloading finished in 542 ms.
  Jul 30 22:21:24 systemd[20455]: Reload requested from client PID 276641 ('test_gc_explici')...
  Jul 30 22:21:24 systemd[20455]: Reloading finished in 551 ms.
  ... four in a row per test binary

Where they come from:
  - lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:122 and :126 — apply_plan frames start/stop with a daemon_reload on each side.
  - lifecycle.ml:176 and :180 — the down path does the same around the file removals.
  - lib/gc/gc.ml:117 and :128 — opportunistic_sweep and purge each add one.

So `pctl up` costs ~2.2s of pure Manager.Reload before any service work, and `pctl up` on a host with a stale registry row adds another. On this machine the user manager's reload is ~540ms because it re-runs systemd-xdg-autostart-generator over the whole autostart dir each time (visible in the same journal window).

The ordering comment at lifecycle.ml:90-102 explains why each reload is where it is, and the reasoning holds — this is not a correctness bug. But the trailing reload of apply_plan and the leading reload of the next command are back-to-back with nothing in between, and gc's sweep reload runs immediately before lifecycle's. Worth checking whether the pairs can collapse.

Note before optimising: measure. 540ms is this host's number, driven by its generator set, not a pctl constant.

comments.author: manveru
comments.text:
Correction to this ticket's own arithmetic, caught in review of pctl-jbd.

The body says 'four Manager.Reload calls per up/down' and cites four 'Reload requested' journal lines per test binary. Those four are one up PLUS one down — each e2e binary does both. Per command it is two:

  lifecycle.ml:120-126, apply_plan — one daemon_reload before the row application and one after. Exactly two.
  lifecycle.ml:154 — reload calls apply_plan once on the up path.
  lifecycle.ml:176,:180 — the down path has its own two.
  gc.ml:117,:128 — two more, but only for a project the sweep actually removes.

So: two per up, two per down, plus two per swept project. ~1.1s of reload per command on this host, not ~2.2s. The finding stands, the magnitude halves.

title: cli: quiet 'pctl down' swallows every exception with a bare 'with _ -> 0'
description:
Pre-existing; found while reviewing the pctl-jbd retry diff.

lib/cli/pipeline.ml:292-296:

    if quiet then
      try
        work ();
        0
      with _ -> 0
    else run work

The bare `_` returns exit 0 for anything: a Pctl_error, a caqti Failure, Unix_error, Out_of_memory, Stack_overflow, and — newly relevant after pctl-jbd — Eio.Cancel.Cancelled, since Dbus.daemon_reload can now yield at a cancellable sleep inside Bus_retry.with_retry where it previously could not.

Inconsistent with the repo's own established practice one module over. lib/gc/gc.ml:65-73 narrows the analogous best-effort catch and says so explicitly:

    (* ... We still narrow from [_] to the specific
     * failure modes we've observed: systemd not running (Unix_error),
     * pctl-tracked errors (Pctl_error), and caqti wrappers (Failure). *)
    let ignore_best_effort f =
      try f ()
      with Failure _ | Unix.Unix_error _ | Schema.Pctl_error _ -> ()

Quiet down plausibly should not fail the caller — that part is a deliberate product choice and is not in question. What is wrong is the width: the catch should name what it tolerates, so an unexpected failure mode is not silently reported as success.

Fix: narrow to the same three constructors gc.ml uses (Failure | Unix.Unix_error | Schema.Pctl_error), and add a comment naming why quiet down returns 0. Decide explicitly whether Eio.Cancel.Cancelled should propagate — it should, so that a cancelled switch is not reported as a clean down.

comments.author: claude
comments.text:
lib/gc/gc.ml has the same shape at three more sites, and pctl-jbd's retry diff made one of them newly reachable. Same fix, so folding it in here rather than filing a duplicate.

  gc.ml:151-155  | Schema.Unknown -> (try remove_project ... with e -> eprintf "failed to sweep %s")
  gc.ml:158-159  with e -> eprintf "pctl gc: warn — sweep aborted: %s"
  gc.ml:175-178  with e -> eprintf "pctl gc: warn — failed to remove %s"

All three bind a bare `e`. These are better than pipeline.ml:296 in that they do print — but like it, they catch everything and continue.

What changed: Dbus.daemon_reload is now a cancellation point. Bus_retry.with_retry calls Eio.Time.Mono.sleep (dbus.ml:564), so Eio.Cancel.Cancelled can now leave daemon_reload where previously the call was a synchronous FFI round trip that could not yield. gc.ml:71-73's ignore_best_effort is correctly narrow and lets Cancelled through — straight into these three catch-alls, which swallow it and carry on iterating rows inside a cancelled context. Every subsequent Eio operation then re-raises immediately, so the sweep degrades into a loop of 'warn — failed to sweep' lines rather than unwinding.

So the fix for this ticket should cover both files and should explicitly re-raise Eio.Cancel.Cancelled (and Stdlib.Exit) rather than only narrowing to the Failure | Unix_error | Pctl_error triple — narrowing alone fixes gc but not the intent, since these three sites want to keep going on a per-row failure and must NOT keep going on a cancellation.

title: gc: opportunistic_sweep's best-effort daemon_reload now inherits a 5s retry budget it then discards
description:
Raised in the review of pctl-jbd and deliberately left for a separate call.

lib/gc/gc.ml:117 and :128 both do:

    ignore_best_effort (fun () -> M.daemon_reload handle)

ignore_best_effort (gc.ml:71-73) catches Schema.Pctl_error and returns unit. Since pctl-jbd, Dbus.daemon_reload retries a peer-gone reply for up to Bus_retry.peer_gone_budget (5 s) before raising. So during a window where the user manager is off the bus, each of those two call sites can now block for 5 s and then throw the result away — per project, inside purge's per-row loop. opportunistic_sweep runs at the top of every mutating command (up/reload/down/restart), so a 'pctl up' issued while a nixos-rebuild is reexecing the manager can sit for 10 s in the sweep before it does any work.

Mitigated but not solved by the same change: the raised error now carries '(gave up after N attempts over X.Xs)', so the exhausted case is at least distinguishable — in a message gc discards. The user still sees nothing.

Worth noting the bound is only reached when the manager does NOT come back, in which case the command's real work fails immediately afterwards anyway. Measured recovery on this host was ~1 s, so the common case costs ~1 s and succeeds. That is the argument for leaving it.

Three options, none obviously right:
  1. Leave it. Sweep reloads are cheap when the manager is healthy and the 5 s worst case coincides with a session that is broken anyway.
  2. Give the best-effort call sites a zero budget, so gc keeps its old fail-fast behaviour and only the load-bearing reloads in Lifecycle retry. Needs a way to pass a budget through the Systemctl port, which today has 'daemon_reload : t -> unit' and no options.
  3. Have ignore_best_effort log what it swallowed instead of dropping it, so a 10 s stall is at least explained. Cheapest, and independently defensible.

Related: pctl-e0d (four reloads per command).

title: gc: the new Reload retry turns a peer-gone window into a silent multi-second stall, because both gc reloads are swallowed
description:
Raised in the pctl-jbd review; the retry diff acknowledges it in a comment but does not fix it, so it needs to be tracked.

lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:570-573 (new):

    (* Say so when the budget was spent, so an immediate rejection and
     * a five-second exhausted retry are distinguishable. Callers that
     * discard the error still get the seconds in the message —
     * [Gc.opportunistic_sweep] swallows this one entirely. *)

That last clause is exactly the problem. lib/gc/gc.ml:117 and :128 both call M.daemon_reload inside ignore_best_effort (gc.ml:71-73), which catches Schema.Pctl_error, so the carefully constructed "(gave up after N attempts over 5.0s)" string is built and then dropped with nothing printed.

Cost, now that the retry exists:
  - remove_project issues two reloads, so each swept row can burn 2 x Bus_retry.peer_gone_budget = 10 s.
  - opportunistic_sweep (gc.ml:140) runs at the top of up/reload/down/restart (lib/cli/pipeline.ml:170, :204), once per Unknown row.
  - purge (gc.ml:163) runs it per non-Live row.

So with the user manager off the bus for a non-transient reason — ServiceUnknown / NameHasNoOwner are in peer_gone_error_names and are NOT necessarily a passing reexec — 'pctl up' gains up to 10 s of dead air per Unknown row and 'pctl gc --yes' up to 10 s per non-Live row, with no output at all. Before the retry these failed instantly (and just as silently).

Two things to decide, separably:
  1. Should gc's reloads opt out of the retry? A sweep is opportunistic; waiting 5 s for a manager that may not come back is a poor trade there, unlike on the lifecycle path where the reload is load-bearing. A ~budget parameter on daemon_reload, or a non-retrying variant, would express that.
  2. Regardless of (1), the swallow should not be total. Every other gc failure path prints 'pctl gc: warn — ...' with describe_exn (gc.ml:151-155, :175-178); ignore_best_effort is the one that prints nothing. Give it the same warn-and-proceed treatment so an exhausted retry is at least visible.

Note the interaction: fixing (2) alone still leaves the stall; fixing (1) alone still leaves it silent.

title: systemctl/dbus: unit_state reports Inactive for ANY Pctl_error from GetUnit, so a bus fault reads as a healthy stopped unit
description:
Pre-existing; found while reviewing the pctl-jbd retry diff.

lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:673-682:

    let unit_state t ~unit:u =
      (* GetUnit may fail with NoSuchUnit for a unit that has never been
       * loaded. systemd's own `systemctl is-active` reports "inactive" in
       * that case, so mirror that. We treat any exception on get_unit_path
       * as "inactive". *)
      match
        try Some (get_unit_path t ~unit:u) with Schema.Pctl_error _ -> None
      with
      | None -> Schema.Inactive
      | Some path -> ...

The comment's justification covers NoSuchUnit and says so; the catch covers every Pctl_error. Same shape as pctl-8za and pctl-2m8, both of which were narrowed to Schema.is_no_such_unit.

Why it matters more than the usual over-broad catch: the value is not discarded, it is REPLACED with a plausible wrong answer. A transport failure, a denied call, or a peer-gone reply all render as 'this unit is inactive' to whoever asked — probe (lib/probe/probe.ml) and 'pctl status' among them. A running service reports as stopped, and nothing anywhere says a bus call failed.

Newly reachable in practice: pctl-xxf establishes that GetUnit (dbus.ml:686) is one of the unretried calls during a daemon-reexec window, where it answers org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.NoReply. So during any NixOS / home-manager activation, unit_state can silently report every unit as Inactive.

Fix: narrow to `with Schema.Pctl_error e when Schema.is_no_such_unit e -> None` and let everything else propagate. Correct the comment to say no-such-unit only. Add an integration case: arm the fake to fail get_unit_path with a non-NoSuchUnit reply and assert unit_state propagates rather than answering Inactive.

Check unit_job_pending (dbus.ml, the Properties.Get(Job) path) for the same shape — a swallowed error there yields 'no job pending', which is the same class of plausible wrong answer.

title: systemctl/dbus: three sites drop bus failures without narrowing, unlike the sibling sites the repo already narrowed
description:
Pre-existing; found while reviewing the pctl-jbd retry diff. Grouped because the fix and the precedent are the same for all three; split if they turn out to want different answers.

The precedent: pctl-8sd added Schema.is_no_such_unit and pctl-2m8 applied it in gc, on the principle that a best-effort site should name what it tolerates rather than catching everything. These three did not get that treatment.

1. lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:596-603 manager_unsubscribe_best_effort — binds `let _rc = ...` and returns unit. The header comment ('systemd may have dropped the connection during shutdown') justifies tolerating a disconnect; the code tolerates every rc including EINVAL and AccessDenied. Weakest of the three: it only runs from close (dbus.ml:426), where there is nothing left to do about a failure. Arguably fine as-is with a comment saying 'every rc, deliberately'.

2. lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:608-617 reset_failed_unit — same `let _rc = ...` shape. Its comment says 'Swallows not-loaded/not-failed errors: callers use this best-effort, same as systemctl --user reset-failed with a glob that matches nothing'. That is a claim about two specific replies, and the code makes no attempt to check which reply came back. A transport failure leaves the `failed` tombstone in place and the caller believes it was cleared. Fix: check rc, tolerate the not-loaded/not-failed names by equality, propagate the rest.

3. lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:802 — `try entry.cb s with _ -> ()` inside the sd_bus_add_match handler, with no comment at all. Silently drops any exception from a subscriber callback, so a bug in a probe callback disappears. There is a real constraint here — an exception must not escape into the C dispatch frame — but 'must not escape' is satisfied by catching and REPORTING, not by catching and discarding. Fix: keep the catch, eprintf the exception with the subscriber's unit name, and say in a comment why it cannot be re-raised.

Related but tracked separately: pctl-a7p (unit_state answering Inactive on any Pctl_error) is the same family but worse, because it substitutes a wrong value rather than dropping an error.

title: docs: the UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE 'host' rule is breached by the repo's own prose, including that file
description:
UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:124 states the rule verbatim:

  - **"Host"** is overloaded: the machine running pctl vs. the allocated `127.0.0.N`. In pctl code and docs, **Host** always means the allocated loopback address; for the machine, use "host system" or "dev host".

CLAUDE.md points at this file as binding ("Read UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md before writing code or docs"), but bare "host" for the dev machine is the norm in prose:

  - UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:88 - **Reality test**: "An e2e test run against the host's real systemd --user"
  - UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:91 - **Straggler**: "A slice left behind on the host session"
  - CLAUDE.md Tests section - "runs the real-systemd suite on the host"
  - lib/systemctl/bus_retry.ml:4,93 - "observed on this host", "Measured on this host"
  - test/e2e/test_reload_survives_reexec.ml:12,21,30 - "on this host"

A rule nothing observes is not a rule. Decide one way and make the docs match: either replace the bare uses with "dev host", or narrow the rule to code identifiers only and say so at :124.

Filed from the round-4 review of pctl-jbd. Pre-existing; the bus_retry/e2e sites are new in that diff but are the same breach as the surrounding prose, so not that diff's job.

title: test/lib: read_file is hand-rolled in four places; the e2e harness should own one
description:
Four near-identical open/Fun.protect/really_input_string implementations, none reachable from the others by dune scoping:

  - lib/cli/init.ml:23-29        read_file (raises on missing)
  - test/unit/test_helpers.ml:7-12
  - test/e2e/harness.ml:172-180  read_unit (same shape, unit-file specific)
  - test/e2e/test_reload_survives_reexec.ml:60-66  read_file (returns "" on missing) -- newest copy

test/e2e links e2e_harness, not test_helpers or cli's internals, so the fifth caller will copy it again. Harness is already the shared library every e2e test links; put a generic read_file there and have read_unit and the new test call it.

Note the copies are not equivalent: init.ml raises Sys_error on a missing file, the new e2e copy returns "". Whichever lands in Harness has to pick one and say why -- the e2e copy's "" is load-bearing for its vacuity guard (an absent marker must compare unequal to "ok", not raise).

Filed from the round-4 review of pctl-jbd. Three of the four copies predate that diff.

title: schema: two more copies of the refuted 'transport failure leaves sd_bus_error empty' claim
description:
The pctl-jbd diff corrected the 'transport failures leave the sd_bus_error struct empty' claim in three places (lib/systemctl/dbus.ml:105-111, dbus.ml:342-347, lib/systemctl/bus_retry.ml:59-72). Two copies outside lib/systemctl were not touched and still assert the refuted version:

  - lib/schema/schema.ml:465 -- '... its decoded-errno fallback for a transport failure -- fail the test, which is the safe ...'
  - test/unit/test_schema.ml:314 -- '(* transport failure: sd_bus_error empty, reply is the decoded errno *)'

What the source actually says (systemd v260, the version this machine runs): every fail: path in sd_bus_call_methodv and sd_bus_call runs sd_bus_error_set_errno, which resolves through errno_to_bus_error_const or falls back to strjoin("System.Error.", name) / BUS_ERROR_FAILED. A transport failure therefore arrives NAMED -- 'System.Error.ENOTCONN' for a closed bus -- not with an empty struct. The empty-struct case is near-unreachable through sd_bus_call_method.

The test at test_schema.ml:314 is not wrong as a test -- it exercises the (None, None) arm, which is legitimate coverage of a total match. Only its comment's description of when that arm occurs is wrong.

Fix: reword both to match lib/systemctl/bus_retry.ml:59-72, and at test_schema.ml:314 say the case is the near-unreachable backstop rather than 'transport failure'.

Filed from the round-5 review of pctl-jbd. Pre-existing: neither file is touched by that diff.

title: gc: nothing ever reclaims a state dir, so StateDirectory data accumulates permanently
description:
Gc.remove_project (lib/gc/gc.ml:93-133) stops the slice + every manifest unit, deletes those unit files from user.control, wipes the manifest and the projects row. It never touches the state dir systemd created from a service's StateDirectory= logical suffix. Neither does `pctl down` (Lifecycle.down, lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:187-191, clears runtime columns only). So `pctl-<project id>-<suffix>` under $XDG_STATE_HOME is write-only: pctl creates the conditions for it and has no path that removes it.

Measured on this host (2026-08-02): 14 such dirs, ~111 MB, against 0 registry rows (`pctl gc --json` -> `[]`, live=0 orphan=0 unknown=0). Ten are ~8.4M postgres data dirs from e2e scratch projects; the largest are pctl-tuor_e96edffc-pg (16M) and pctl-scratch_tuor_a02abe4c-pg (11M).

Design constraint the empty registry exposes: a reclaim that hangs off row removal cannot help here. With no rows, nothing maps any of the 14 dirs back to a project, so all of them are already past rescue. A working sweep has to enumerate $XDG_STATE_HOME/pctl-* by NAME and cross-reference the project id embedded in it against the registry — which is close to the pre-SQLite gc design UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md used to describe (state dirs classified by cross-reference), except the cross-reference target is a registry row rather than a known marker.

Open questions for whoever takes this:
- Is deleting a state dir ever in scope for gc, or is durable service data something pctl should refuse to delete and only report? A postgres data dir is not obviously garbage just because the project row is gone.
- If reclaim is opt-in, what is the surface — `pctl gc --state-dirs`, a separate confirmation, or report-only always?
- Unparseable/foreign `pctl-*` dirs under $XDG_STATE_HOME need a class of their own; the current Unknown means "project path is gone", not "no owner found".

Surfaced while fixing pctl-oik (the UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE gc rewrite). Not fixed there: that ticket was docs-only, and this is a product gap with an undecided policy.

title: e2e harness: teardown leaks one state dir per scratch project, ~8.4M per run
description:
Each reality test gets a unique tmpdir -> unique project id -> unique slice (CLAUDE.md Tests section). That same uniqueness applies to the state dir: a service declaring StateDirectory = "pg" renders to pctl-<project id>-pg, so every run of every such test creates a fresh directory under $XDG_STATE_HOME.

Harness.teardown (test/e2e/harness.ml, run via with_scratch) takes the project down and clears the failed tombstone on its slice. It does not remove the state dir, and `pctl down` cannot do it either (Lifecycle.down clears runtime columns only). The tmpdir goes away; the state dir named after the id derived from that tmpdir stays forever.

Measured on this host (2026-08-02): ten pctl-project_<hash>-pg dirs, ~8.4M each, plus pctl-scratch_tuor_a02abe4c-{pg,server}. So `scripts/e2e-repeat.sh 5` costs roughly 42 MB of postgres data dirs that nothing will ever collect.

The harness owns these dirs — it knows the project id it derived — so teardown can remove them by name without waiting on the gc policy question in pctl-gc-state-dir-reclaim-bd1. Suggest teardown enumerate $XDG_STATE_HOME/pctl-<its own id>-* and remove those, and only those: the sandboxing rule is that a test touches nothing outside its own project id.

Note the ten leaked ids are all distinct, so there is no accumulation-in-place to reuse; the count grows linearly with runs.

Depends on nothing in pctl-gc-state-dir-reclaim-bd1 — that one is about user-facing reclaim policy, this one is test hygiene the harness can fix unilaterally. Surfaced while fixing pctl-oik.

title: state/db: default_path falls back to "/" when HOME is unset, silently siting the registry at /.local/state/pctl/state.db
description:
lib/state/db.ml:27-39:

  let default_path () =
    match Sys.getenv_opt "XDG_STATE_HOME" with
    | Some d when String.length d > 0 -> d
    | _ ->
        let home =
          match Sys.getenv_opt "HOME" with
          | Some h when String.length h > 0 -> h
          | _ -> "/"      <-- here
        in
        Filename.concat home ".local/state"

With neither XDG_STATE_HOME nor HOME set, pctl opens /.local/state/pctl/state.db instead of failing. ensure_parent_dir (db.ml:41-50) then mkdir -p that path, so on a writable root it succeeds and every project silently registers in a second, invisible registry; on a read-only root the user gets an mkdir error naming a path they never configured.

Contrast the sibling reader: Clock.read_boot_id_exn (lib/clock/clock.ml:8-12) deliberately raises on a blank read rather than degrading, with the reason at the line. Same class of input, opposite policy.

Fix: raise when both vars are absent/empty, naming both env vars in the message. There is no identity value for "where is the state database" — "/" is a plausible wrong answer where raising reports the bug.

Found while reviewing pctl-oik (UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md registry rewrite): UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:41 documents the fallback chain as ending at $HOME/.local/state/pctl/state.db, so the doc does not describe this third level either. Fixing the code removes the need to document it.

title: docs: .claude/skills/pctl still documents the pre-SQLite registry and the pre-v2 @@PROJECT@@ placeholder
description:
The bundled pctl skill teaches two models the code no longer implements. Both mislead a reader who follows the skill instead of UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md.

1. Registry is described as ephemeral runtime-dir state.
   - .claude/skills/pctl/TROUBLESHOOTING.md:15 — "the registry entry was lost (typically because $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR was cleared on logout and the slice is no longer running anyway)".
   - TROUBLESHOOTING.md:17 — "If the slice is actually running but the registry entry is gone, systemctl --user stop pctl-<id>.slice is a last-resort fallback".
   - SKILL.md:35 — "up ... writes a fresh registry entry".
   The registry is now SQLite at $XDG_STATE_HOME/pctl/state.db (lib/state/db.ml:27-39). The row survives logout and reboot; a session reset (lib/state/session.ml) NULLs only host/started_at/spec_file/session_id, and only gc deletes the row (lib/gc/gc.ml). So the TROUBLESHOOTING diagnosis is now a wrong conclusion, not just stale wording: "row is gone" no longer follows from "you logged out".
   Term is "registry row", not "registry entry" — UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:42 lists "Registry entry" as an alias to avoid.

2. @@PROJECT@@ is documented as live behaviour.
   - SPEC.md:71 — "Any literal @@PROJECT@@ in a unit's filename or body ... is replaced with the project id at install time".
   No code path substitutes it: grep across lib bin nix test templates finds it only in three comments recording its removal (nix/lib/mkProject.nix:14, lib/render/render.ml:3, test/e2e/harness.ml:58). The replacement is the logical suffix (UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:46, expanded in lib/render/render.ml). SPEC.md:63 states the expansion correctly, so :71 also contradicts its own file.

Fix: rewrite TROUBLESHOOTING.md:15,17 against the SQLite/session-reset model, s/registry entry/registry row/ in SKILL.md:35, delete SPEC.md:71.

Found while reviewing pctl-oik. Out of that ticket's scope: it is confined to UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md.

title: lifecycle: after a reboot, pctl up starts nothing — the durable manifest matches the re-rendered units, so every row is Unchanged
description:
Derived by reading code, not executed — no repro run. Every step below cites the line that settles it.

Scenario: `pctl up`, then reboot without `pctl down`.

1. The manifest survives the reboot. `Session.reset`'s `reset_query` (lib/state/session.ml:15-22) NULLs only `projects` columns (host, started_at, spec_file, session_id). The `manifest` table is untouched; its only other writers are `Gc.remove_project` and `Lifecycle.reload` itself.

2. The unit files do NOT survive. `Unit_store.Fs` roots at `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/systemd/user.control` (lib/unit_store/fs.ml:30), which is tmpfs. After the reboot there are no unit files and no running services.

3. `up` is `reload ~spec:(Some spec)` (lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:181-182). It compares the persisted manifest against a freshly rendered one — `manifest_before = Projects.load_manifest`, `manifest_after = WA.run` (lifecycle.ml:129-136). `diff_manifest` (lib/state/projects.ml:177-199) compares stored hash to rendered hash and never consults the filesystem.

4. The rendered bytes are identical to last boot. Unit content is a pure function of (spec, project id, host, project path) — `Write_all.run` (lifecycle.ml:66-85), `service_dropin_body` (lifecycle.ml:55-59). No timestamp, no boot id. The host is re-allocated to the same value: `Host_alloc.allocate` is `(md5_first_byte id_s mod 253) + 2` (lib/identity/identity.ml:58) and `taken` is empty because session reset NULLed every host.

5. So every plan row is `Unchanged`, and `apply_row` (lifecycle.ml:111) matches `Unchanged -> ()`. `apply_plan` issues two `daemon_reload`s and starts nothing.

Result: `pctl up` writes the unit files, prints "project <id> up · N units · host=127.0.0.N", exits 0, and zero services are running. Recovery requires `pctl down` (which empties the manifest via `reload ~spec:None`) and then `up`.

Not covered by tests: test/e2e/harness.ml gives each test a fresh XDG_STATE_HOME, so no test ever sees a durable manifest with an empty user.control. test/integration/test_state.ml:137,158 exercise `reset_with_boot_id` at the state layer only.

Same failure without a reboot: delete a project's files from user.control by hand, then `pctl up`.

Candidate fixes (not decided): have the session reset delete the manifest rows of every project whose session it clears — the units it names provably no longer exist — or have `up`/`reload` treat a manifest entry with no file on disk as `Added`. The first keeps the filesystem out of the diff; the second makes the diff honest about disk state.

Found while reviewing pctl-oik (UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md rewrite). It also falsifies the glossary line "Session id … Equal to the current boot id ⇒ the project was started on this boot": the stamp happens in Pipeline.with_project (lib/cli/pipeline.ml:184-192) before Lifecycle runs, so this path marks the row Live while starting nothing.
design:
Decided by grill 2026-08-03. Fix = D1: the diff's left side comes from disk, not from SQLite.

## Reference check (read locally, not recalled)
home-manager a184bd2 (2026-03-30), sd-switch bc44b75, nixpkgs 6242698 (2026-06-12).

- Both take the "before" side from FILES, never a DB. sd-switch loads $oldGenPath/home-files/.config/systemd/user (systemd.nix:534) and byte-compares (lib.rs:128-137); switch-to-configuration parses old_unit_dir.join(unit) (main.rs:1170,1285).
- Both put cross-invocation bookkeeping on tmpfs. s-t-c's resume lists are /run/nixos/{start,restart,reload}-list (main.rs:68-70), and $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nixos for user scope (main.rs:175-188).
- Neither owns the start decision. Both drive the plan loop from live systemd state (lib.rs:111-115; main.rs:1157,1229) and let WantedBy= plus active-target restarts start new units (lib.rs:133-136; main.rs:1239-1266).

pctl deliberately took the other side of that trade: fs.ml:5-7 picks user.control precisely because it disappears across reboots. So pctl owns the start decision, and must not keep the ledger in a longer-lived store than the thing it describes.

## Shape
- `manifest` keeps its name and its table; migration 004 rebuilds it without `sha256` (rebuild rather than ALTER TABLE DROP COLUMN, so it does not depend on the linked SQLite version). It now records ONLY ownership: which unit filenames this project may delete. load_manifest/replace_manifest change to Unit_filename.t list, which is a compile error at each of the 34 call sites across 10 files — the intended loud break.
- The unit->hash map becomes its own type, and the pure diff moves out of state/projects.ml:171-202 into lib/plan/ as `Plan.diff ~installed ~rendered`. test/unit/test_manifest.ml follows it. "rendered", not "desired": pctl stays a differ, so the right side names its provenance (lib/render/) rather than asserting a claim about reality.
- `installed` = for each OWNED name, US.read the main + drop-in and hash via the existing hash_entry. Read owned names ONLY, never the union with rendered — otherwise a leaked unowned file on disk hashes as Unchanged and never starts, which is this bug re-entered from the other side.
- Write_all splits into a pure Render_all plus a write step.
- The file-removal set is `owned \ rendered_names`, NOT the diff's Removed rows: a unit whose main file vanished but whose drop-in dir survived produces no Removed row, and the drop-in would leak.
- Ownership persists two-phase: `owned U rendered_names` before the writes, `rendered_names` after the removals, both before apply_plan. Invariant: the manifest always names a superset of pctl's files on disk. This closes two leaks — US.write raising mid-loop (Install_failed: ENOSPC/EACCES), and start_unit propagating from apply_row (lifecycle.ml:112) before replace_manifest (:181) ever runs.
- Unit_store gains `read : t -> unit_:Unit_filename.t -> entry option`; In_mem.inspect is promoted to it. None means the main file is absent, and nothing else — any other errno raises Install_failed. A lenient `with _ -> None` would turn a permissions fault into "restart everything, every run".
- Fs.write with dropin=None must delete an existing drop-in dir. fs.ml:74-77 currently returns without touching it while In_mem.write replaces the whole entry, so the adapters already disagree; in_mem.ml's header claims it mirrors Fs's observable semantics. read . write = id becomes load-bearing here: without it a stale slice drop-in makes the slice permanently Changed on every reload.
- lifecycle.ml:40-49 gets deleted. It documents a one-time hash-formula churn against stored hashes that will no longer exist.

## Why not the alternatives
- Clearing manifest rows in Session.reset fixes only the reboot trigger and leaves the class open (hand-deleted files stay broken). It also keys the fix on boot id; D1 needs no boot id at all.
- Deleting the manifest table entirely (filesystem fully self-describing via PCTL_ID in the drop-in) needs two ownership rules, one of them a parse of a generated file, and makes gc's correctness depend on a drop-in that could have been half-written.
- Making `up` a reconciler (Unchanged requires unit_state = Active) was rejected: Schema.kind includes Oneshot and mkProject.nix:106 always forces Type=, so it would re-run every oneshot and every genuinely-failed service on each invocation. up and reload are the same function (lifecycle.ml:184-185), so they cannot be given different convergence semantics without breaking "reload is the only primitive".

## Behaviour changes to note
- A user editing a unit file inside user.control by hand now surfaces as Changed and self-heals, where today it was invisible.
- Post-reboot `pctl up` now prints `+N` rows where it printed `=N`.
acceptance_criteria:
## Tests

Integration (test_lifecycle.ml, whose header at :5-6 already earmarks exactly these):
- reboot: up -> Session.reset_with_boot_id ~boot_id:"boot-2" -> fresh empty In_mem store -> up -> every row Added, every unit started.
- hand-delete: up -> US.remove one service -> up -> that unit Added, the rest Unchanged.
- superset invariant: fail_next_write -> up raises -> the manifest already names the units written before the failure.
- persist ordering: fail_next_start -> up raises -> the manifest is persisted anyway.

Unit:
- Fs: write {dropin=Some _} -> write {dropin=None} -> read gives dropin=None. This is the ONLY place the Fs defect is catchable; In_mem never had it, so every fake-backed test is blind to it.
- Plan.diff relocated from test_manifest.ml, behaviour unchanged.

E2E (new test, template = test_down_missing_units.ml):
- up -> assert active -> `systemctl --user stop <slice>` -> rm the unit files and .d dirs from user.control -> daemon-reload -> pctl up -> is-active reports active.
- The stop is REQUIRED. Deleting a unit file kills nothing (measured in test_down_missing_units.ml's header), so without it the services stay active, `up` no-ops on an already-active unit, and the test passes without ever exercising a start — a test that cannot fail for the right reason.
- Test header records what a real reboot changes that this does not (boot id, host reallocation, systemd's loaded-unit set) and why none of it is load-bearing under D1.

Gate: dune test green; dune build @e2e --force green; scripts/e2e-repeat.sh green.

## Docs (same commit — these lines become false the moment the code lands; pctl-oik is closed, so they land here)

- UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:29 Manifest — no longer "{unit-filename: sha256} snapshot ... used as the left side of the next reload diff". It is the set of unit filenames a project owns, persisted in the registry, and it is the authority for what down and gc may delete. The left side of the diff is read from user.control per invocation.
- :41 Registry — amend "plus its manifest rows" to say what those rows now hold.
- :73-76 Reload diff — "present in new manifest, absent in old" becomes "present in rendered, absent in installed". The added(+) row's ACTION changes under pctl-added-restarts-g31, not here.
- :105 rule — "up writes one Registry row and one Manifest; reload reads the Manifest" no longer describes the flow.
- :121 dialogue — "The new spec file produces a new manifest. Diffing against the stored manifest ..." restates the removed design.

title: state/db: the foreign_keys pragma is never enabled, so manifest's ON DELETE CASCADE is inert
description:
migrations/001_init.sql:12-17 declares `manifest.project_id ... REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE`. SQLite enforces foreign keys only when `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` is set per connection; State.Db.connect does not set it, and no migration does either.

Consequence today: benign. Gc.remove_project already wipes the manifest by hand (lib/gc/gc.ml:130-131) immediately before deleting the project row (:132-133), so nothing depends on the cascade firing. The declaration is decoration that reads as an enforced invariant.

Two ways out, not decided:
  - set the pragma on connect and delete the manual wipe, so the schema statement becomes the single source of truth;
  - drop the REFERENCES clause and keep the manual wipe, so the code is the only claim.

Either is fine; having both, with one of them false, is not.

Found while designing pctl-468 (manifest -> ownership-set). Not blocking it: that work rebuilds the manifest table in migration 004 and can carry whichever clause is chosen.

title: lifecycle: two concurrent pctl runs on one project race on user.control and the manifest, with no lock anywhere
description:
Nothing serialises two pctl invocations against the same project id. No advisory lock on the state db, no lock file in user.control.

Real today, not hypothetical:
  - `pctl up` racing `pctl down`. Lifecycle.reload's down arm removes every unit file it owns (lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:177-179) while the up arm is writing them (:137 via Write_all). Whichever calls State.Projects.replace_manifest last (:181) wins, and the surviving manifest can disagree with what is actually on disk in either direction: files present that the manifest does not name (never removed by a later down or gc) or names with no file.
  - two concurrent `up`s are mostly benign only because Render is deterministic, so both write identical bytes.

pctl-468's D1 design adds a read of user.control before the write, which is the first time a run's decisions depend on what a *concurrent* run has put on disk: an installed-hash can now be read from a half-written file. It does not create the race, and the two-phase ownership persist agreed there keeps the manifest a superset in both interleavings, so this stays P3 rather than blocking.

No repro run — derived from the absence of any locking call in lib/state/db.ml and lib/unit_store/fs.ml.

Options if it is ever worth fixing: a per-project advisory lock (flock on a file in user.control, or BEGIN IMMEDIATE held across the lifecycle body). The second is simplest but holds a write txn across systemd round trips, which pctl-e0d measures at ~540ms each.

title: lifecycle: Added must restart, not start, when the unit is still running
description:
Under pctl-468's D1 fix, `Added` stops meaning "this unit is new" and starts meaning "no file on disk". Those are not the same, because deleting a unit file kills nothing — measured and recorded in test/e2e/test_down_missing_units.ml's header (fragment gone, unit still loaded, processes still running).

Repro: hand-rm a service's unit file from user.control, edit the spec, `pctl up`.
- `installed` has no hash for it -> Added
- apply_row calls start_unit (lib/lifecycle/lifecycle.ml:112)
- systemd no-ops because the unit is already active
- the process keeps running the OLD config; pctl prints `+` and exits 0

Today the same case yields Changed -> restart_unit and is handled correctly, so D1 regresses it. The information to distinguish "new" from "vanished but running" is not recoverable: the file was missing, so there is no installed hash, and no query to systemd reveals what the vanished file used to contain.

## Fix
services: `Added -> restart_unit`. slice: `Added -> start_unit` (unchanged).

RestartUnit on an inactive or unloaded unit simply starts it, so this is identical to today for genuinely-new units and for the whole post-reboot path (nothing is active there). Zero extra D-Bus calls. Querying unit_state on Added rows was considered and buys nothing, since restart-on-inactive already IS start.

Cost: a spurious bounce when a file vanished, the content would have matched, and the service was healthy. Accepted — a spurious restart is visible and self-correcting, a stale process is neither, and reaching it requires a manual rm against a running service.

## The slice carve-out is not symmetry
`restart` on an active slice cascade-kills every service in its cgroup. Delete only pctl-<id>.slice and leave the service files intact: the slice goes Added -> restart -> every service dies, while the services are Unchanged -> not restarted -> the project is entirely dead and `pctl up` reports success. Strictly worse than the bug D1 fixes. Same hazard lifecycle.ml:96-99 already documents for Changed on a slice, so is_slice_unit gains a second use rather than a new concept.

## Docs
UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:73 defines "Action: added (+)" as `start`. It becomes `start` for the slice, `restart` for services.

## Tests
- integration: unit already active + file absent + rendered bytes differ -> assert restart_unit was called, not start_unit.
- integration: slice active + slice file absent -> assert start_unit, never restart_unit, and that no service was stopped.
acceptance_criteria:
Tests:
- integration: unit already active + file absent + rendered bytes differ -> restart_unit called, not start_unit.
- integration: slice active + slice file absent -> start_unit called, never restart_unit, and no service stopped.

Docs (same commit):
- UBIQUITOUS_LANGUAGE.md:73 "Action: added (+)" is `start` for the slice and `restart` for services.

title: state: manifest FK cascade is inert — no PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON
description:
migrations/001_init.sql declares

  project_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

on the `manifest` table, but SQLite enforces foreign keys only when `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON` is set per connection, and I see no such pragma in State.Db.connect. So the cascade never fires.

Nothing depends on it today: lib/gc/gc.ml:130-133 wipes the manifest manually with replace_manifest ~rows:[] immediately before delete_by_id, which is why the inert constraint has never been noticed.

Found while designing pctl-468. Not fixed there — that work rebuilds the manifest table (migration 004) and carries the same clause across unchanged, so the situation is neither improved nor worsened by it.

Decide: either set the pragma at connect and drop gc's manual wipe, or delete the REFERENCES clause so the schema stops claiming an integrity guarantee it does not provide. A declared-but-unenforced constraint is the worse of the three states.
close_reason: duplicate of pctl-fk-pragma-inert-kcl, which was filed first today with the same two-ways-out framing

title: lifecycle: two concurrent pctl runs on the same project race on user.control
description:
Two `pctl` processes invoked on the SAME project path (same project id, same slice, same unit filenames) have no mutual exclusion. Nothing in Pipeline or Lifecycle takes a lock; State.Db is a per-invocation caqti connection.

Today the overlap is write-then-persist: both render, both write the same unit files, both replace_manifest. Because the rendered bytes are a pure function of (spec, id, host, project path), two runs of the SAME spec converge; two runs of DIFFERENT specs (one mid-edit) can interleave writes and leave the manifest describing bytes neither run wrote.

pctl-468's D1 widens the window on the read side: `installed` is now derived by reading user.control before the write, so run A can read, run B can write, and run A then diffs against bytes that no longer exist and applies a plan for a state that is gone.

Not addressed in pctl-468 — that work makes the read explicit but does not create the race, and serialising it is a separate design decision (advisory flock on the project's slice file in user.control, a SQLite lock held across the invocation, or an explicit "already running" refusal).

Note that different projects do NOT race: ownership and unit filenames are project-id-scoped, so their file sets are disjoint. This is strictly about concurrent invocations on one project.
close_reason: duplicate of pctl-concurrent-runs-race-xn5, which is more thorough (covers up-racing-down) and already accounts for D1's two-phase persist
